OPEN SIX BUTTON


Text: 阿難白佛言世尊。如來雖說第二義門。今觀 世間解結之人。若不知其所結之元。我信是世間解結之人,若不知其所結之元。我信是人終不能解。

Transcription: Ananda told the Buddha: World-Honored One, the Tathagata preaches the second meaning. The golden contemplation of the world resolves the cause of binding, but if one does not know the origin of the binding, one's self and the other's faith cannot be resolved.

Vietnamese translation: Ananda told the Buddha: World-Honored One, although the Tathagata has taught about two decisive meanings. Now look at the people in the world who want to untie the knot. If you don't know where the knot is, then I'm sure those people can't untie it.

Lecture: After listening to what the Buddha explained above, Ananda had other doubts, so Ananda had another reason, wanting to find a place where there was no more reason to doubt. So Ananda asked the Buddha, "World-Honored One, although the Tathagata has taught about two decisive meanings." This speaks of two decisive meanings, one case is to use the mind of the conditioned mind, the object of birth and death, to practice and the other case is not to use the mind of the conditioned mind, the object of birth and death, to practice.

Now look at the people in the world who want to untie the knot, if they don't know where the knot is – if they don't know where the knot is – then I'm sure those people won't be able to untie it. Since they couldn't even identify the clue to the button, how could they open it?

Text: 世尊我及會中。有學聲聞亦復如是。從無始際與諸無明俱滅俱生__TA G3__,雖得如是多聞善根。名為出家。猶隔日瘧。

Transcription: The World-Honored One visited the middle-right community to learn the sound of writing and the heron to serve as thi. Following waterless sacrifices to the data of ignorance and cessation of birth, yet attaining such a multi-literate good root. Famous for becoming a monk, traveling around the world.

Vietnamese translation: World-Honored One, I and the Thanh Van friends in this assembly are the same. From beginningless time until now, we have been born and died together with all kinds of ignorance, even though we have good roots to hear the Buddha's teachings like that. Even though they are called monks, they are like people who have malaria every other day.

Lecture: Ananda is very straightforward. He has a peaceful and innocent personality like a child, he is very simple. World-Honored One, I and the Thanh Van friends in this assembly are also the same. The third level of Arhatship is called 'Learned.' When the fourth level is reached, it is called Uneducated. "We Shravakas are like people trying to open a knot; we don't know where the clue is, where to untie it? The Buddha said that we can use the six faculties, but which one should we start with? Which one is the most difficult to open? Right now we don't understand."

From beginningless time until now, we have been born and died together with all kinds of ignorance. From beginningless kalpas until now, we have been born and have died, creating one karma in this life and another karma in the next life. In this life you believe in Buddhism, but in the next life you won't believe it anymore. Or maybe in this life you don't believe in Buddhism, but in the next life you will. Or maybe you believe in Buddhism, but don't truly understand it. You are confused and just want to know. In that way, we cannot separate from ignorance. It should be said that people are bound by family or wife and children. But not only that. What we are bound to is ignorance. Ignorance for you is like a shadow following an image; it follows you wherever you go. It never leaves you even for a moment. It's even more intimate than those who just got married.

Ignorance follows you during birth and death; This is clear evidence for why eternal ignorance is inseparable from you. It doesn't mean that when the husband dies, the wife dies with him. In exceptional cases this may happen, but it is not the rule. Only ignorance will die with you and will be reborn with you. This is truly going together in life and inseparable in death. It takes up half of what you call yours, like a shadow following a figure.

And of course, do you know that what concerns us is ignorance? If you know ignorance, then don't be intimate with them anymore. If you don't understand ignorance, it's best to find out quickly. If you understand ignorance, there will be some hope for you. If you do not understand ignorance, then you will forever be an ordinary person. If you understand ignorance, then you are halfway to sainthood. But you must really understand clearly, don't act like you understand but don't understand anything, making it seem like you have ignorance and don't have it.

Even though he has good roots, he can hear the Buddha's teachings like that. Although it is called a monastic product. Our penchant for multiliteracies is a form of goodness; but although he is called a person who lives according to monastic conduct, he is like a person who has malaria every other day. The characteristic of this disease is that it manifests every other day, at a certain time of day. This example symbolizes Ananda's ignorance. Today Ananda is no longer ignorant, his mind is clear, he is no longer delusional. But tomorrow ignorance arises again. I believe that it is not only Anan who encounters this problem. I polled everyone present here, everyone had similar problems.

Today you develop bodhicitta and decide to practice the path, so you single-mindedly practice meditation. “I didn't pay attention to what happened, ignored everything.” But tomorrow you won't be able to ignore it. Once again, you pick up the things that you usually get stuck on and can't let go of. Even if you want to let it go, you can't let it go. Do you feel pitiful? That is what it means for someone to have malaria every other day. So you should quickly find a way to cure this disease for yourself.

How to cure? Drink lots of wisdom water. Once you have wisdom, you will naturally see through things and let them go. When you can let go, you will feel at peace. Why do you have this disease? Because you value your body so much, with its physical satisfaction and natural well-being, you always have a plan on its behalf. So you cannot see clearly and let it go. But no matter how beautiful a body you have, it will still rot the moment it dies. No one wants to come closer anymore.

Text: 唯願大慈哀愍淪溺。今日身心云何是結。從何名解。亦 令未來苦難眾生。得免輪迴不落三有。

Transcription: Duy vow pronoun ai introspection. The sun, body, mind, clouds, and rivers are connected, and the river of fame and fortune is connected. Sentient Beings will be exempt from reincarnation and will not be in the three states of happiness in the future.

Vietnamese translation: May the Great Compassionate One have mercy on those who are drowning. Now, right here in our body and mind, please show us how to tie the knot and how to open it. It also causes Sentient Beings to suffer in future lives to escape samsara and not fall into the three realms.

Lecture: Ananda is truly pitiful. Please pray for the Great Compassionate One, World-Honored One, to have great compassion for us. We are the ones who are drowning. Now, right here in our body and mind, please show us how to tie a knot. We have sunk so deeply into ignorance that we are not aware of what our body and mind are like. Which of the six bases should you choose to start opening the knot, and which should be last? If you are the one who will open these buttons, you must open them right from the beginning. You can't grab the middle to do it and expect it to open. I don't know why it opened. Where do we open from? Asking the Tathagata to explain will make Sentient Beings–I not only ask for myself. I have developed the mind of Supreme Bodhi and want Sentient Beings to suffer in their future lives so that they can escape samsara and not fall into the three realms. If they know the method of opening knots, they will not fall into the three realms. They will escape suffering in the Desire Realm, Form Realm and Formless Realm.

Text: 作是語已,普及大眾 五體投地,雨淚翹誠,佇佛如 來無上開示。

Transcription: Tathagata's language popularizes the five bodies of the first earth, Vu Li Kieu Thanh, stores the Supreme Buddha Tathagata Dharma Talk.

Vietnamese translation: Having said those words, Ananda and the assembly planted five feet close to the ground, crying sincerely, looking forward to hearing Tathagata's supreme Dharma Talk.

Lecture: Having said these words, after Anan made a request, he and the assembly planted five meters close to the ground. The five dimensions are two legs, two arms and head. Weeping sincerely, Ananda cried like rain – do you know why Ananda was so weak? From the beginning of the Dharma teaching conference until now, Anan has cried six times, including this time. Now when listening to this sutra preached, no one cries. Are you all stronger than Ananda? Ananda heard the teachings of Shakyamuni Buddha and when he deeply understood that teaching, Ananda cried. This time Anan cried very intensely, like rain. Ananda's tears are probably enough to wash his face.

"Looking forward" represents Ananda's enthusiastic mind. Maybe this word (佇 hoa – anticipation) is the origin of women's high heel shoes. They saw that Ananda was so sincere that he had to stand on his toes and they decided to walk around in that position. Looking forward to hearing Tathagata's supreme Dharma Talk.

I just said that now everyone is better at listening to sutras than Ananda, but nevertheless, you should not think that you are really better than Ananda. Honestly, I'm just making fun of you!

You will speak. ‘Oh!’ Why does the master have to make fun of the disciple?’

If I didn't mock you, you wouldn't have the courage to diligently practice. Ananda cried because he was too enthusiastic to seek the Dharma - extremely enthusiastic. Ananda realized that even though he had attained Arhatship, he still did not fully understand the Dharma, so Ananda felt very regretful. That's why Ananda cried so bitterly. And why don't you cry? I will answer for you. It's because you are not interested in Buddhism. You do not focus on Buddhism.

‘It's not like that.’ You say: “I actually study very diligently every day.”

That doesn't count, because you don't let the Buddha Dharma enter your mind - in your mind. If that were the case, you would cry every day. Now my disciples often like to cry, they realize that they have just been freed from bondage. “I could continue to cry every day because I don't understand Buddhism.” But those of you who want to cry should not cry. You should be self-controlled and calm. Anyone who doesn't want to cry should feel ashamed and ask themselves, "Why don't I understand the Buddhadharma?" If you can cry because of that, cry with regret like Anan here, then there is still some chance for you.

Those who don't know how to cry, they can try. Those who do not want to cry cannot be forced to do so. And those who like to cry cannot cry. That's how Buddhism works.

Those who go too far should hold back a little. Those who have not gone far enough should exert themselves a little more. That is the ultimate meaning of the Middle Way.

Text: 爾時世尊憐愍阿難。及諸會中諸有學者。亦 為未來一切眾生。為出世因作將來眼。

Transcription: At the time of the World-Honored One's hearing, Ananda, referring to the scholars in the assemblies, all sentient beings of the future were sentient beings, with the eyes of future human beings appearing in the world.

Vietnamese translation: At that time, the World-Honored One took pity on Ananda and the learned people in the assembly, and also for Sentient Beings in future lives, created a cause to appear in this world to serve as a spiritual eye for future lives.

Lecture: At that time, Ananda requested the Buddha to give him the ultimate Dharma Talk. The World-Honored One took pity on Anan and the learned people in the assembly. 'Learned class' refers to the first three stages of Arahantship: Sotapanna, Sotapanna, Anahamma. Also because Sentient Beings in the future life, 'future life' is only for us today; We are Sentient Beings in the future. Creating a cause beyond the world – this is a special cause. ‘Worldly’ is only for ordinary people. Those who have appeared in the world are the Shravakas – Arhats – Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas and Buddhas. Because they help Sentient Beings transcend this world and become the eyes of the path for the next life, so that they can be the eyes of the path for all Sentient Beings in the future. Buddha did very rare things.

Text: 以閻浮檀紫光金手摩阿難頂。即時十方普佛世 界六種振動。

Transcription: Di match-pu-dan purple light golden head demon Ananda peak. Immediately, the six-species Buddha world of the ten directions shook.

Vietnamese translation: The Buddha used his golden hand, shining like a matchstick, to rub Ananda's head. At that moment, the Buddha realms in the 10 worlds all vibrated.

Lecture: The Buddha used his hand, bright and golden like a matchstick, to rub Ananda's head. The Buddha's arm has the yellow color of the matchwood tree in Southern Thiem region. In Buddhism, rubbing the head with your hand symbolizes compassion and protection. At that moment, the Buddha realms in the ten worlds all vibrated. The six types of world shocks have been explained before. When a person practices enlightenment and achieves Buddhahood, there are six types of shocks that occur. During the Dharma Ending Age, when someone practices and attains the Noble Path, six types of shocks also occur. There are many reasons why the six types of concussions occur. When demons and pagans want to harm someone, they can also create a commotion, but it does not necessarily belong to these six types of concussion. There are countless types of vibrations caused by heavenly demons. For example, there was a recent earthquake in the Philippines, which was reported to have killed 400 people. I thought that was an estimated statistical number.

I think at least 500 or 600 people died. That disaster is a karmic retribution of Sentient Beings, causing demons and pagans to destroy this human world. That's what happens whenever there's a natural or man-made disaster. But if there is a High Monk with pure conduct in the place where the disaster is about to happen, For example, in the Philippines, or if there is a Bodhisattva or Arahant who has attained enlightenment in that place, then the disaster can be dissipated. When a practitioner has pure morality, they can even go into places that are in danger, they can turn bad things into good things; they can turn difficulties into advantages. They can make dangerous situations pass peacefully.

The six types of vibrations are: shock, roar, shock, vibration, noise and rise. The three types of head concussions are acoustic. The following three types belong to movement. Vibration is a very strong vibration. The sound is pushed upwards, like a large wave rising into the middle of the sea. To start is to suddenly rise, like an elevator.

When there is an earthquake, there is a loud sound. One day right here in San Francisco there was an earthquake, all the windows began to break. "Danger! Danger!" Everyone shouted. I noticed someone passing by was so scared that he clasped his hands together. The others saw this and immediately followed her. The collapse creates sound, but when there is a roar, there is a cry inside that sounds like the roar of a lion. Clicking is the sound that resonates when the ground is split into two pieces and then collide with each other.

What do the six types of tremors symbolize? Why did the earth tremble in six levels as described in the Shurangama Sutra, when Buddha rubbed Ananda's head? That's because the Buddha was about to present a very important teaching. The Buddhas in the 10 directions all praised him with just one sound. That's one case. Also symbolizes the freedom of the six senses – untying the six knots. Ananda just asked about the origin of these six knots and how to open them. Ananda asked where to start and which button should be opened last. The Buddha was about to explain this doctrine, so the Buddha rubbed Ananda's head and six vibrations occurred on the earth.

Text: 微塵如來住世界者,各有寶 光從其頂出。

Transcription: Tathagata's microscopic dust resides in the false world, and all the precious lights appear at the same time.

Vietnamese translation: The Tathagatas are as numerous as the number of motes in the worlds, all of which have precious halos emitted from their heads.

Lecture: The Tathagatas are as numerous as the number of motes in the lands–innumerable Buddhas–they are in the lands. Each Buddha resides in each of his Buddha lands. Each Buddha has a precious halo emitting from his head. Each of the countless Buddhas emitted rare rays of light from their heads. There is a red aura, there is a white aura, there is a yellow aura, there is a blue aura - all the auras are emitted from the crown of the Buddha's head. The Tathagata Buddhas, as numerous as the number of dust particles, emitted countless rays of light to represent the wonderfulness of the teachings that the Buddha was about to present and symbolized that the teachings were extremely sublime and profound, the teachings that emanated from the Great Buddha's birth.

Texts: 其光同時於彼世界 來祇陀林, 灌如來頂。是諸大眾得未曾有。

Transcription: Wonderful light at the same time, the hybrid world of Ky-da forest, contemplation of Tathagata peak. May the great assembly attain the position of monks.

Vietnamese translation: That halo simultaneously came from the other realms, reached the Ky-da forest, and poured down to the Tathagata's temple. All the masses here are getting something unprecedented.

Lecture: At the same time, the aura that the Tathagata has as many as the number of particles emitted from the top of his head, from those realms - from the land where the Buddhas are residing - to the Jeta forest. Note that these are rays of light that are projected towards the Jeta forest, not the Buddhas themselves. The radiance from each Tathagata was as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River and as numerous as the dust particles, pouring down onto the crown of the Tathagata, Shakyamuni Buddha. This symbolizes that the teachings of the Tathagatas are the same. The dharma this Buddha preached is also the dharma that this Buddha proclaimed. Are identical. Light is interdependent and Sentient Beings' minds are also interrelated. The aura of the Buddhas is inherently interconnected, so the aura is the Buddha mind.

Same nature with the mind of Sentient Beings. If you are upset with someone, that person will know immediately, even if you don't say a word. It's not that that person knows intentionally, on the level of the sixth consciousness (consciousness), there is inherently discrimination, but there is an induction from the 8th consciousness. The other person has knowledge from the 8th level of consciousness because the human mind inherently has the nature of interdependence. Today's science has discovered this, that there is an invisible relationship, like telegraphy, that can communicate with each other very quickly even though they are very far apart. And the human mind has a system of mutual telegraphs. It cannot be seen with the naked eye, but if you truly have perfect understanding and attain the unobstructed Buddha eye, then you will clearly see why you know thoughts arise in the minds of others. That's because the other person sent a telegram. If you have opened the Buddha eye or wisdom eye, then you will naturally recognize and be able to see that.

Because of these telegrams, people can immediately recognize when you have thoughts of dissatisfaction with them. Your telegram arrives, and in time it becomes upset with you. Some people have sympathy for others, and that's the same, the other person also knows that sympathy, but it is responded to more slowly. If you want to influence others for transformation by means of positive influence, then you should use good ideas to influence them, but the process will be slow step by step. Gradually you will make them awaken. When they awaken, their behavior will be positive again.

Now that I have explained how this telegraph system operates between you two, there will be people who will not believe what I say. However, it is true. In the future, when you truly open the Buddha eye, you will no longer have any doubts about this teaching. Then you will realize, "Oh! I didn't believe it then, but it's true." All the halos poured down on the Tathagata's head, symbolizing the unity of the teachings of the Buddhas and the projection of halos between the Buddhas. The ultimate Dharma that the Buddhas preach is identical.

All the masses here are getting something unprecedented. No one understood what they saw happening. "Ah! Why do the Buddhas in the 10 directions release light and pour it down onto our Buddha's head? What does it symbolize?" Can you imagine why there are countless rays of light emitted by Tathagata Buddhas as numerous as motes? The halos are countless and incalculable. But it's not confusing at all. Each beam of light shines very clearly on Tathagata's head. Those who have opened the Buddha eye, those who have attained the first three stages of Arahantship, do not understand what they see. Even those who have attained the fourth stage do not fully understand it. The reason they don't understand is because they have never seen this happen before. “Getting something unprecedented” means they have never seen anything like this happen before.

Text: 於是阿難及 諸大眾俱聞十方微塵如來異口同音告阿 難言。

Transcription: U Thi Ananda mentioned to the masses the sentences from the ten directions and dust of Tathagata's different words with the same sound as Ananda's words.

Vietnamese translation: At that time, Ananda and the crowd all heard the Tathagatas in the 10 directions as numerous as dust particles telling Ananda in unison.

Lecture: At that time, Ananda and the great assembly, the Great Bodhisattvas, the Great Arhats, and the Great Bhikkhus, all heard the Tathagatas in the ten directions as numerous as dust particles. All of these have become one, each one is a part of the whole. At the same time, they all heard the Tathagata telling Ananda in unison: Even though it was spoken by many people, the sound was consistent. What they said was not only for Anan but also for you, me and those who are listening to the sutra lecture today. This teaching is a very important part of the Shurangama Sutra. It is related to a key point: the problem of birth and death. If you understand this chapter, you can quickly end the cycle of birth and death. If you cannot understand, then you must redouble your efforts and diligence in studying.

Text: 善哉阿難。汝欲識知俱生無明 使汝輪轉生死結根,唯汝六根更無他物。

Transcription: Kind ear Ananda! Desires and knowledge lead to ignorance, and the cycle of birth and death leads to roots, only the six senses have wings and no other things.

Vietnamese translation: How wonderful, Ananda! He wants to know that the question of ignorance is the clue that causes him to reincarnate in life and death. It is his six senses and not anything else.

Preach: These words make the matter absolutely crystal clear. It's as simple as it is. If you truly understand now, you will be liberated immediately. If you do not understand, you must study carefully. The Tathagata Buddhas in the ten directions, as numerous as the grains of dust, spoke in unison to Ananda, first of all praising Ananda. “How wonderful, Ananda!” Just like how people encourage children. "You're a good kid. You're so good, you're so smart!" First praise and encouragement to attract attention. And when there is attention, the Buddhas will reveal the true meaning. “Anan! You are very smart, because you want to know how to avoid ignorance.

He wanted to realize the true principles of ignorance that had been present in him since birth.” That is also talking about "giving birth to ignorance." It is the clue that makes him reincarnate in the six realms of samsara, bobbing up and down, being born here, dying there, then being born again, then dying again in another place. In this life one can be born as a Westerner, but in the next life one is born as a Chinese person, then in the next life as a Japanese person, then in another life as an Indian, and in the next life as an Indian; The next generation will be Africans. Who is the agent that brought you into this world? Who can know to inform others that they will be Japanese in their next life? Who can tell others that they will be Chinese?

Who can tell others whether they will be Eastern or Western, or Northern or Southern? Nothing other than your ignorance can do that. Because of ignorance, people develop delusion, and because of ignorance, karma is created. Because of creating karma, one must suffer retribution. For example, “In this life I must go to Africa. There are a lot of diamonds there. There is more wealth on the Gold Coast than in America. No one has excavated there yet, I will go there to invest, I will be rich, right? I will be the richest man in the world.” From that false thinking, you created a false trip that ended in Africa, to develop the Gold Coast and search for diamonds.

Those who like America will go to America, those who like Australia will go to Australia, those who like Europe will go to Europe, those who like Asia will go to Asia. It's up to you. No matter what karma you create, you must receive that retribution. You go there as a human being and once you get there you don't know what happened. And so you don't know what you'll be aiming for next. The dream of getting rich has disappeared, but you still haven't awakened. It's pitiful, isn't it? The dream of getting rich never ends. When it comes to death, the search for diamonds is not finished, but life is exhausted.

It is your six senses and nothing else. The roots of samsara become knotted into a knot from which you cannot escape. What is that? It is nothing more than a deception of your eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and mind. These six things cause your dog to be born and die. Do you know that? There is no one else responsible. What makes us go crazy, born again and again, then death after death, is simply our six senses.

What's up? The eyes see physical objects and are then turned around by them. Listen to sounds and then follow them. The nose smells the scent and becomes attached to it. The tongue tastes the delicious flavor and then indulges in it. The body enjoys touching and then pursues the object it comes into contact with. The mind is interested in the dharma and pursues it. Tell me, how many things do you absolutely have? So many. Following the six senses, you become divided into six parts. You are like a company with six businesses that each take a small amount of money until the company goes bankrupt. So the company had to die young. Bankrupt. Collapse, vanish.

With the small amount of capital you just lost, you are confused about where you will go to open another company. So you go everywhere to open a new company. And in the new place you do the same thing as before. The six bosses of their new businesses hoped they would do a good job, but they didn't, and the job ended. That is where the problem of birth and death arises. Previously in the sutras, the Buddha advised, “You just don't follow it.” You should not follow the discriminating mind. You should not pursue the activities of the six senses, six objects, and six consciousnesses. Don't follow them, turn towards the shore.

Suffering brings suffering
Turn around and see the shore.

Turn around and see the shore of enlightenment. If you don't turn around, the more confused you become, the deeper you fall into confusion. The deeper you go into confusion, the more confused you become. You owe a lot of money, and your accounts never balance. Now that you have recognized the six senses, you should not accept the enemy as your child. Don't rotate around that six sense axis anymore. Let's go back. Come back. Where to? Go to the lecture hall to listen to Buddha's teachings.

Text: 汝復欲知無上菩提令汝速登安樂解脫寂靜妙常__T AG3__,亦汝六根更非他物。

Transcription: The supreme Bodhisattva of enlightenment, the speed of peace, peace, liberation, tranquility, wonderful eternity, the green heron's wings fly away from all things.

Vietnamese translation: You also want to know that Supreme Bodhi makes you quickly liberated, peaceful, peaceful, and wonderfully quiet, that is also your six senses, nothing else.

Lecture: Right before this sutra passage, the sutra says that it is the six senses that cause you to experience the cycle of birth and death, causing ignorance to arise, creating karma, and having to suffer retribution. But you should not underestimate the six senses. You cannot say, "You six hateful things! I will gouge out my eyes and throw them away. I will cut off my ears and throw them away. I will cut off my nose and tongue. That's right, I will cut my body into parts and crush my bones and flesh into one. I will cut my heart into small pieces and spread them into space, returning them to boundless nothingness."

That attitude is also a mistake. People who have already developed the mind to cultivate the Way should not develop anger. Even if your eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind don't treat you well - just like in a business - they are all embezzlers, you still cannot get rid of them. Why not do that? Because, even though they are not good now, they will help you if they change. If they don't act as embezzlers, they will help you get rich.

This sutra says that if you become enlightened and attain the true nature of eternal wonder, peace and tranquility, it is brought about by the six senses. It is to be grateful to them for making it happen.

This is similar to the example of water and ice. Water can be in liquid or solid form, it can also benefit or cause harm to humans. So you shouldn't get angry and you shouldn't say that we don't need our ears and eyes anymore. If you don't need your eyes anymore, you become blind. If you don't need your ears anymore, you become deaf. If you don't need your nose anymore, then you become a strange person. If you don't need your tongue anymore, you won't be able to speak, and if you don't need your body anymore, you won't achieve anything, you will return to emptiness. You can't do anything without spiritual training. Therefore, the Buddhas in the 10 directions now say to Ananda: "You also want to know the method to open the knots, right?"

Please note that these two Chapters of the Sutra are not only preached by Shakyamuni Buddha. It is precisely because the Buddhas in the ten directions, as numerous as the dust particles – countless and boundless Buddhas – now speak to Ananda. 'Very good, Ananda, you are a sincere person. He is truly a person who is sincere in his practice. You also want to know Supreme Bodhi.'

The word 'bodhi' here refers to the cause of practice to attain enlightenment. It should not be understood as bodhichitta in this case. It means 'You also want to develop the mind of Supreme Bodhi to achieve Bodhi, so that you can quickly be liberated, peaceful, peaceful and wonderful.' I think here people understand the word 'quickly' as quickly becoming a Buddha as soon as possible. The four virtues of nirvana are mentioned in this sutra. 'Peace' is true happiness, and 'freedom' is the quality of the true self. If you still have a self, you cannot have freedom. If you want to achieve liberation, you must eliminate that ego. 'Silence' symbolizes 'truth'. ‘wonderful permanence’ symbolizes true permanence. "These are the four virtues of Nirvana without residue, and are also your six senses, nothing else. Ananda, do you realize it?"

But after the Buddhas in the ten directions had taught this Dharma, Ananda still did not understand. When you are in confusion, even if someone else explains it wisely, you still cannot figure it out yourself. "Then what is the meaning of it? The cycle of birth and death is caused by the six senses, but to practice enlightenment, liberation and attain enlightenment, it is also from the six senses. How are these six senses expressed, through what is good, through what is bad? Ananda does not understand, but people can be both good and evil. Nowadays, some people feel they are good, want to help people. "I want to help the poor." He thought so and took the money and gave it as alms. But the next day he gave up that thought, "Yesterday I gave a lot of money, today I don't want to waste it like that anymore, I will use a gun to rob it." So he became a bad person. It's also him. Who is the creator of evil? It's also him.

I want to emphasize to you that the same person who becomes a devil, the same person will become a Buddha. Because most Americans don't believe in ghosts. So why do we become demons even though we don't believe in it? Because I'm not a devil, I can't talk about it. If you believe in Buddha, then you should also believe in ghosts. In general, Buddha also came from demons. If you do good deeds, you will become a Buddha. And if you do evil things, you will end up as a ghost. Using the same metaphor as above, the six senses cause you to suffer the cycle of birth and death; The six senses also help us attain enlightenment. If there were no demons, there would be no humans, and there would be no Buddha. There will be nothing, and the world will come to ruin. Those who say they believe in Buddha but do not believe in demons are too shallow, so even if Buddha appeared in the world, he would not be able to educate them. The Buddha clearly taught in the scriptures that there are demons, why don't you believe that they exist?

You have the opinion, "Other religions also talk about demons!" But you don't have your own definitive opinion, that you believe there is no devil just because other religions say so. The reason other religions talk about demons is because demons are real. Just because you don't believe in other religions, doesn't mean you reject all the truths in their doctrines, such as the existence of demons. Many people think they are smart but actually they are very dumb. Not just because they do not understand Buddhist teachings, but because they do not understand human existence. How pitiful!

Text: 阿難雖聞如是法音,心猶未明。稽首白佛:__TAG7_ _云何令我生死輪迴安樂妙常同是六根,更非他物 ?

Transcription: Ananda's writing is like the sound of Dharma, his mind is clear. Khe Thu said to the Buddha: The clouds, the spirit, the self, the cycle of birth and death, peace and joy, are always the same as the six senses, the wings and wings of other things?

Vietnamese translation: Even though Ananda heard the Dharma sounds like that, his mind was not clear. Bowing his head, he asked the Buddha: "Why is it the six senses that cause me to suffer the cycle of birth and death, and it is also the six senses that cause me to be eternally peaceful and wonderful, and not something else?"

Lecture: Ananda heard Shakyamuni Buddha and the Buddhas in the ten directions as many as there are particles of dust, saying in unison that the root of the cycle of birth and death is the six senses, and the root to obtain everlasting wonderful and pure happiness is also the six senses and nothing else. But Ananda did not understand. Even though Ananda heard the sound of the Dharma like that, Ananda heard the inconceivable wonderful sound of the Dharma, but his mind was not clear. And because my mind was not clear, I bowed my head and said to the Buddha – Ananda bowed my head to pay respect to the Buddha – Why is it the six senses that cause me to suffer the cycle of birth and death – spinning forever in the cycle of birth and death – and it is also the six senses that cause me to have eternal wonderful peace – Ananda mentioned both the issues of permanence and happiness – and not something else? You don't understand this principle?

Text: 佛告阿難,根塵同源__TA G6__,縛脫無二。識性虛妄猶如空花。

Transcription: Buddha announced Ananda, the roots of the earth are the same, the blessings are incomparable. Consciousness is illusory due to being flowerless.

Vietnamese translation: The Buddha told Ananda: "The base and the ceiling are the same root, binding and loosening are not two. The nature of consciousness is illusory, like a flower spotted in the void."

Lecture: The Buddha told Ananda: "The base and the ceiling are of the same origin." The six senses, six objects, and six consciousnesses all have the same root. If there were no six senses, there would be no six senses; If there were no six sense objects, there would be no six consciousnesses. All three are one, one and three. Binding and loosing are not two things. 'Tie' refers to the knot, 'open' refers to the untying. These two things are not two (non-dual). There is no fundamental difference between them. Wisdom is open, open is binding. When you don't understand, it's binding. When you understand, it's liberation, the knots have been untied. It all depends on your abilities. The nature of consciousness is illusion. The nature of the six consciousnesses is that they have no definite form. Like a spotted flower in the middle of nowhere. Do you still remember the person who suffered from itchy eyes? Due to looking for a long time, it turned out that my eyes were tired and I saw strange flowers in the void. It is completely unreal. If you see something beautiful, it also turns ugly. Likewise, humans can be both good and evil. Although 'good' and 'evil' are two different words, they both refer to the same person.

Text: 阿難,由塵發知,因根有相。相見無性,同於交蘆。

Transcription: A-nan, developed by the world, causes have roots and forms. The general view has no nature, it is the same as the lot.

Vietnamese translation: Ananda, knowing (of the senses) arises from the world, and from the senses comes appearance (of the world). Both appearance (part of perception) and view (part of perception) have no self-nature, like bunches of reeds stuck together.

Lecture: Ananda, from the worldly place, knowledge (of the senses) arises. Discriminating knowledge arises because of the six sense objects. Because of the senses, there is the appearance (of the ceiling). The appearance of the six senses arises because of the six senses. Both appearance (part of perception) and view (part of perception) have no self-nature, like bunches of reeds stuck together. The view (part) here refers to the sense (object of knowledge; e: sense-awareness) as mentioned first. Both appearance (part of the view) and view (part of the faculty of view) have no inherent nature. The form appears only because the six senses unite with the six senses; because it's not real; it is completely illusory. Views are also false. It is 'like a bunch of reeds leaning against each other.'

The bunches of reeds here show a common root, from which two reed stems grow. It can only stand if they are two, one stalk will fall if the other stalk falls. The six senses, six objects, and six consciousnesses are similar. The senses and objects must work together to create the six consciousnesses. One thing alone will not stand. Another metaphor, a bunch of reeds is like a deep hole, so when you look down, it seems like there's something in there, but there's absolutely nothing in there. That symbolizes the illusory nature of the six senses and six senses.

Text: 是故汝今 知見立知即無明本。知見無,__TAG5_ _見斯即涅槃。無漏真淨。云何是中更容他物?

Transcription: Thi co Nhu kim, immediate knowledge means original ignorance. Views without views, thoughts are truly pure nirvana without outflows. Van ha thi middle wing winged things?

Vietnamese translation: So now you yourself, right in the place of knowledge, establish the form of knowledge, that is the root of ignorance. In the place of knowledge, if there is no form of knowledge or knowledge, then that is pure nirvana without asrava. How could there be anything else in there?

Lecture: So now you, right in the place of knowledge, establish the form of knowledge. You establish another view on top of the knowledge that is already false. That is the root of ignorance. In the place of knowledge, if there is no form of knowledge or knowledge, then that is pure nirvana without asrava. He realized that his knowledge was inherently without substance, so he did not generate any thoughts based on that knowledge. Even in that knowledge, not giving rise to any discriminatory thoughts is in accordance with the Tao. That is the true pure nirvana of anasrava. How could there be anything else in there? In the absence of knowledge, how can there be anything else? That place is the pure source of the Dharma Realm. Why would you want to put something else in there? Why add knowledge on top of knowledge? This principle is the same as said in the previous sutra passage, "Original enlightenment is wonderful wisdom, but it is false so it becomes clear enlightenment."

Texts: 爾時世尊欲重宣此義, 而說偈言:

Transcription: At the time of the World-Honored One, he wanted to repeatedly declare the meaning, while he preached the verses:

Vietnamese translation: Now the World-Honored One wanted to repeat this meaning, so he recited this verse:

Lecture: Now Buddha Shakyamuni, you know that Anan still does not understand the answer to Anan's question, so the World-Honored One wants to repeat this meaning, so he speaks this verse. The verse has a certain number of syllables in each line, which can consist of 5, 6 or 7 syllables in Chinese.

Text:真性有為空, 緣生故如幻, 無為無起滅, 不實如空花。

Transcription: True nature is finite and unconditioned, Dependent birth is as illusory, Unconditioned and non-arising, Unreal as flowerless.

Vietnamese translation: In terms of true nature, conditioned dharmas are empty. Because of dependent origination, they are like illusions. Because all dharmas are unconditioned, they are neither born nor destroyed. They are not real, like flowers in the middle of nowhere.

Lecture: On the aspect of true nature, that means on the aspect of the absence of all illusions. Emptiness, however, depends on true nature to exist. Therefore, conditioned dharmas arise from true emptiness. But the nature of conditioned dharmas is emptiness (śūnya).

Because of dependent origination, they are like illusions. Conditioned dharmas arise when conditions meet. But, when causes and conditions arise, they will also disappear. Therefore, the essence of dharmas is emptiness (śūnya). That is why it is said that dharmas are illusory.

Because all dharmas are unconditioned, they are neither born nor destroyed. You think that the nature of conditioned dharmas is empty, so what about unconditioned dharmas? Is their nature empty? That's right. They are neither born nor destroyed.

They are not real, like flowers in the middle of nowhere. They do not have a certain entity; they are unreal, like spotted flowers in the middle of nowhere.

Texts: 言妄顯諸真, 妄真同二妄, 猶非真非真, 云何見所見?

Transcription: False words show all truths, False truths are the same two hopes, Because of non-truths and non-truths, What is the view of Van Ha?

Vietnamese translation: Talking falsely to reveal the truth. False truth is false. (Truth) is neither true nor non-true. How can one have the ability to see and understand?

Lecture: Talking falsely to show the truth. Why do we talk about falsehood? That is to show that all dharmas are true. But truth and illusion are opposites, so they are not ultimate dharmas. In The Dao Ca, Master Huyen Giac said:

The truth is not established, the original emptiness is false,
Existence has no control, no non-emptiness.

There is no such thing as truth. The illusion is inherently empty, but the truth is also not real. What is called a leg? The leg did not exist. There is also no existence or non-existence. You have to make nothing empty: this is the same principle. The illusion is said to show the truth. But the truth and illusion that you talk about are all illusion. They are not real. If they are real, how can there be falsehood in them? There is nothing in there: it is the vacuum of the dharma realm. That is the 'one true dharma realm', 'the true dharma realm.' In it, not a single dharma is established. As soon as you talk about truth by comparing truth with falsehood, truth immediately becomes false. The leg that is being talked about is no longer the original leg. Both are false because they treat each other.

In the field of salvation, Buddhism is absolute; there is no duality. Truth and falsehood are still on opposite levels and fall within the category of duality. The truth that treats falsehood is itself false.

(Truth) is neither true nor non-true. The Buddha preached that it is as if it were true, but it is not ultimate truth. As soon as there is a name assigned to it, it is already the second truth, not the first truth.

How can one have the ability to see and understand? How can you say you have the ability to see and understand? The subject of the 'perception' and the six object objects of the 'appearance' are what are perceived - nothing can be said about them, because they do not exist.

Texts: 中間無實性, 是故若交蘆, 結解同所因, 聖凡無二路。

Transcription: Intermediate with no real nature, Thi Co Nhieu Giao Lo. Conclusion of the same cause, Holy mortal has no two paths.

Vietnamese translation: (Consciousness) is in the middle (senses and objects), has no real nature. So they are like bunches of reeds tied together. Tying and opening are the same thing. Holy and profane are not two paths.

Lecture: In the middle, there is no real nature. Between the true and the false – the six senses, the six objects, the six consciousnesses – truly have no self-nature. So they are like bunches of reeds tied together. Tying and opening are the same thing. When you don't understand, it means you are tied in knots and cannot be untied. When you understand and become free, you see that the cause of both the knot and the untying are the same. If you don't understand, it's called forcing. When you understand, it's called opening. Holy and profane are not two paths. Saints and ordinary people are not two different paths. A saint is one who has understood the principles of all dharmas. They have understood all aspects of the entire dharma realm, so they have the wisdom of saints. Ordinary people, when they do not understand anything, turn their backs on the enlightened nature and associate with afflictions and defilements. Therefore, the practice of ordinary people is the state of enlightenment in the world. The saint is the one who is enlightened and enlightened.

If you turn your back on the clear enlightened nature, you will become one with the defilements and defilements of conditioned dharmas. But, basically, saints and ordinary people are not two different paths.

Why aren't their paths different? One side is confusion and the other side is awareness. But the source of confusion and enlightenment are one. Here we are talking about ultimate truth:
Non-necessary dharma
Ly necessarily general.

Text: 汝觀交中性, 空有二俱非, 迷晦即無明, 發明便解脫。

Transcription: Nhu contemplation of neutral nature, Non-existence of duality, Delusion means ignorance, Invention of convenient liberation.

Vietnamese translation: Look at the nature of the intersecting reed stems, It is not nothing and existence. Being confused about that meaning means ignorance. Understanding that meaning means liberation.

Lecture: Ananda, look at the properties of intersecting reed stems. Observe closely the reed stalks leaning against each other–especially the nature between them. What properties do reed stems have? Nothing. There is nothing clearly visible in the middle. It's not about no and yes. You can say that it is empty, but there is also something there. You may say it exists, but in reality there is nothing. The intersecting reed stems symbolize the non-existence (non-existence) of both conditioned and unconditioned dharmas. You should pay attention to this point.

Being confused about that meaning means ignorance. What it means is that with your six senses, when you do not realize, when you are not aware, then you are confused about emptiness. Confusion arises from emptiness, that is where ignorance arises. In the true mind, pure nature resides, confusion arises and becomes ignorance. Understanding that meaning means liberation. If you discover this, there is no more ignorance. You invent your own enlightened and enlightened nature. This discovery is liberation.

In the past, there was a monk who practiced Zen. He heard that a monk was enlightened with the highest morality. That monk immediately went to the Zen master to ask for Dharma Talk. In Buddhism, praying for Dharma Talk is common. It's not a matter of asking a random question and then being met with a random answer. Since Dharma Talk is given with the aim of ending the cycle of birth and death, the whole matter is thoroughly examined. First of all, the most important thing is that you must bring your robe, seat, and cushion with you. When you arrive at the Zen master's residence, you put on your robes properly, spread out your meditation equipment, pay respects to the Zen master three times, and then fold your hands on your knees. Then you ask questions about things you don't understand.

What did the monk ask? He asked how to be liberated. He wishes to be free. How to be liberated. That was the question he wanted to ask the Elder Venerable, who was an Elder with high morality and seniority in the Sangha.

The monk replied: "Venerable sir, please tell me how I can be liberated?"
The Venerable asked again: "So who is tying you up?"
With that answer, the consulting monk became enlightened. Is it really possible that just one sentence can make a monk enlightened? It's both true and it's not.
You will ask, “What does that mean?”

In almost every case, things are viewed from both sides, and interpreted in many different ways.

“Is that just a way of speaking vaguely or vaguely?”

Not so, if you really want to mention the morality you are concerned about. In this case, we can say that it is true that only one sentence brought enlightenment to the monk, because when the old Zen Master said that sentence, he understood the causes and conditions and made the monk come to the point of asking how to be liberated. The old Zen master knew his answer: “So who is tying you up?” will help the monk immediately realize – enlightenment. Therefore, the old Zen Master chose to answer that way. However, there are times when people are not enlightened, even though the teacher wishes to be so. This time, the old Zen Master was successful with his answer and helped his disciple attain enlightenment.

On the other hand, how to explain that, in just one sentence, enlightenment was brought to the monk? Normally, this monk basically meditated every day to develop his concentration. He has practiced for many years but is still not clear. However, every day this monk still diligently practiced and increasingly developed his wisdom. Although we have not yet truly achieved enlightenment, we are close. Then the Venerable's answer was the fate that helped the monk suddenly realize enlightenment. The monk met all the predestined conditions, and at that moment the old Zen Master Dharma Talk gave him, he immediately realized. These are:

Ten years of meditation in the deserted mountains,
It's not as good as a word of advice from a master.

‘Master’ means ‘one with clear eyes’, one who has acquired the ‘Buddha eye.’ Such a wise man can clearly see causes and conditions. He can preach the Dharma in such a way that it can cause the cause and effect to ripen. So you can meditate for 10 years in a deserted mountain, but it's not as good as meeting a master to initiate you.

Therefore, in Buddhism, being close to a master is very important. Among the elder Zen masters, there are very few who are truly enlightened masters. Maybe they are wise people, but they are not necessarily 'sighted', that is, they have not necessarily 'opened the five eyes.' You should not think that this is an easy thing to do. Indeed, opening the Buddha eye is certainly not the same as achieving Arhatship, but requires you to plant many good roots in the past.

To have the Buddha eye, you must single-mindedly practice the dharma of great compassion, especially the 42 Greatly Compassionate Hands and Eyes (Forty-two Greatly Compassionate Hands and Eyes). If you practice this dharma enthusiastically, you can attain Buddha's eye. That is the method of 'going beyond the gate.' If a person who has attained the Buddha's eye becomes a monk, he will help many Sentient Beings, but it all depends on causes and conditions. Those who want to obtain the Buddha eye must be extremely diligent in cultivating Volume 42 Great Compassion Eye Seal Dharma. Don't give up your practice even for just one day. And the most important thing is that you must not smoke while practicing this method. If you still smoke while practicing, the dharma-protecting good spirits will reprimand you. So don't do it casually.

I hope that everyone here will be very diligent in cultivating Volume 42 of the Great Compassion Eye Seal Dharma. Never be negligent even for a day. However, it takes several years of effort to achieve results. If you have practiced in your previous life, your progress will be very fast. You will very soon have the wisdom eye.

Texts: 解結因次第, 六解一亦亡, 根選擇圓通, 入流成正覺

Transcription: Solve the second fetter, Six solves the first heron perishes, Choose the path to clear the path, Enter the stream to attain enlightenment.

Vietnamese translation: Open the right knot according to the class. When the six knots have been opened, one is no longer left. In the senses, choose the nature of perfect penetration. To enter the stream, that is, attain perfect enlightenment.

Instructions: Open the right button according to class order. It is necessary to follow the order when opening the buttons.

You will ask: "How to untie each knot in order? How is the first knot tied?"

To begin with, the nature of the Tathagatagarbha is not inherently subject to birth and death. But darkness and confusion create nothingness (remorse for emptiness). Right there ignorance arises. Therefore, although the Tathagatagarbha's nature is neither born nor destroyed, relying on the truth gives rise to delusion, and accordingly the mind that is the object of birth and death arises - that is consciousness. This consciousness is divided into the sixth consciousness, the 7th consciousness, and the 8th consciousness. But the source of the 8th consciousness, which originates from ignorance, creating things that arise and pass away, is the nature of the Tathagatagarbha, and this Tathagatagarbha's nature is not subject to birth and death. Its root is the true mind that permanently resides in the pure nature.

Due to relying on the truth to arise, the Tathagatagarbha's nature turns into Alaya consciousness, that is, the 8th consciousness, also known as store consciousness.

The 8th consciousness is the basis of existence of the five aggregates: form, feeling, perception, mental formations and consciousness. Because of the first arising of the aggregate of consciousness, there is the aggregate of volitional formations. This is the 7th consciousness, which is Mana consciousness, also known as transmission consciousness. This consciousness conveys information from the sixth consciousness into the eighth consciousness. It is it that forms the aggregate of volitional formations.

The next aggregate is the aggregate of perception; This is the sixth consciousness, also known as consciousness. The aggregate of feeling is one of the first five consciousnesses: eye consciousness, ear consciousness, nose consciousness, tongue consciousness, and body consciousness. Feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, action aggregate, consciousness aggregate, each corresponds to a knot. The aggregate of form is considered two nodes, because it is more dense. Thus, the six nodes begin with the 8th consciousness and operate through the 7th and sixth consciousnesses and then through the five sense consciousnesses. With the existence of the five aggregates, the five impurities are formed, creating countless obstacles.

If we want to open these knots, we must first stop chasing after the aggregate of form. Once these two nodes have been opened, the other aggregates such as feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional aggregate, and consciousness aggregate are also stopped, the six nodes are all opened. “The knots must be opened in order,” because the form aggregate is composed of gross knots, while the other aggregates, feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, volitional aggregate, consciousness aggregate are extremely subtle.

“So why do they start their formation from the inside and then proceed to the outside?” You will wonder.

Because the 8th consciousness is the first consciousness that gives rise to thoughts of discrimination. Everything originates from the 8th consciousness. The Five Aggregates and the 8th consciousness combine closely to form the knot that binds the cycle of birth and death. Because it starts from the 8th consciousness, when opened, it must start from the aggregate of form. This order is the same as when taking off clothes, you have to take off the outer layer first and then the inner layer. In this way, you take off each layer until the end, like buttons being undone. That's the way to explain it, but the reality is that if you untie one button, the other five buttons will also be undone. As the verse says:

When six buttons have been opened, one is gone. When the six senses, that is, the six nodes, are freed, the one also disappears. This will be explained in detail in the following paragraphs.

In the senses, choose the characteristic of intelligence. The method of practice is to apply effort right from the entrance of the six senses. That is, the eyes are not turned by forms, the ears are not turned by sounds, the nose is not turned by fragrances, the tongue is not turned by tastes, the body is not turned by touches, the consciousness is not turned by dharmas. You immediately transform what appears at the door of the six senses. You reflect back the light, no need to seek outside. Just protect your body and mind. Find it within yourself

To practice in the six senses, you must choose one sense to lead to perfection. Buddha laid the foundation for this method. He explained the 1,200 uses of each sense and showed Ananda which sense was the most complete. For example, the eye faculty is incomplete, but the ear faculty is. The tongue and mind are also complete senses. There are apartments that are complete and there are apartments that are not. You must choose a base and practice diligently on that base. Shakyamuni Buddha implicitly said that the ear faculty would lead to perfect penetration. The Buddha expected Ananda to make his own decision in choosing; Buddha wanted Ananda to find his own decision.

Self-select a perfect faculty and enter the stream, that is, attain perfect enlightenment.

Enter into the dharma realm of the saints. Against the flow of birth and death of ordinary people.

Only after entering the Stream (Enter Stream) can one achieve perfect enlightenment.

Texts: 陀那微細識, 習氣成暴流, 真非真恐迷, 我常不開演

Transcription: Da-na is subtle, habit energy becomes explosive flow. True non-true truth is deluded, Self often does not manifest.

Vietnamese translation: A-da-na consciousness is very subtle. (Causes) habit energy to flow like a rushing stream. I'm afraid that it will be mistaken for true or not true, so the Tathagata often does not mention

Lecture: This is the teaching that the Buddha rarely talked about. “The Tathagata rarely explains this whole matter to you.” Just imagine: Shakyamuni Buddha explaining this Dharma to the Great Arahants, Great Bodhisattvas, and Great Bhikkhus. Yet now we have the opportunity to hear the wonderful Dharma preached by the Buddha himself!

Ananda consciousness is very subtle. This is a very subtle consciousness, even more so than the 8th consciousness. A-da-na consciousness is also called 'White consciousness.' It is the pure seed. (Makes) habit energy flow like a rushing stream. This sensitive and subtle consciousness specifically creates habit energy that flows like a rushing stream of water. This is the source of the cycle of birth and death. As soon as a false thought arises in the one true aspect of this subtle consciousness, it is an ignorant thought; When it returns, it causes habit energy to rise and flow like a rushing stream. Nothing can stop this flow of habits. The rushing water here symbolizes our cycle of birth and death. Birth and destruction, life and death, life after life, sometimes as humans, sometimes as animals, sometimes as Sentient Beings in heaven, sometimes in hell, spinning endlessly - that is the habit energy flowing like a waterfall.

I'm afraid it will be mistaken for true or not true
So Tathagata often does not mention it

"Why does the true Dharma not talk about this issue? Why does the Tathagata not demonstrate this wonderful and true Dharma to you? The Tathagata is afraid that Sentient Beings will consider the true to be an illusion, and make the false to be true. For example, you keep wanting to 'clarify' your 'nature', so you only increase the delusion, on top of the delusion, pile more delusion and become twice as ignorant."

"Normally, the Tathagata does not expound this wonderful teaching. The Tathagata only preaches the Hinayana dharma to those disciples whose faculties are compatible with the Hinayana. The true and wonderful Mahayana dharma is something that the Tathagata has never said before. The Tathagata has not said it because you are people of the Hinayana nature and do not have enough faculty to listen. You have not changed your wish from the Hinayana to the Mahayana, so every time the Tathagata wants to explain this dharma, the Tathagata has to delay it."

Text: 自心取自心,非幻成幻法, 不取無非幻,, 非幻尚不生, 幻法云何立 是名妙蓮華 金剛王寶覺如幻三摩提.

Transcription: One's own mind grasps one's own mind, Non-illusory dharma becomes illusory dharma, Non-illusory non-clinging, Non-illusory dharma is not born, Illusory dharma is empty? The name of the wonderful lotus flower, the precious jewel of the Vajra king. Like illusory samadhi,

Vietnamese translation: One's own mind accepts one's own mind Which is not illusory, but becomes an illusory dharma. Without grasping first, there is nothing non-illusory. Non-illusory does not give birth to the illusory Dharma, how can it be established? That's called the wonderful lotus flower, Vajra King of Jewels

Lecture: Accept your own mind. Sentient Beings inherently do not recognize the view and appearance which are only manifestations of the mind,

The three worlds are idealistic. All dharmas are only conscious.

Unable to recognize the dharmas that appear from the mind, one returns to clinging to views; It means accepting one's own subjective concept – the 8th consciousness. The general part is only for the external environment. The original appearance and the view are both illusory. They are just false images in our minds. Many people cannot believe that they will return to their self-reflective nature, but they only look for it outside. As for the true mind, they are confused and chase after illusion. If you realize that all things are just manifestations of your own mind; if you

Consciousness from the original mind. View from the original nature

Then you will understand that appearances and views originally arise from your mind. If you realize that your true mind permanently resides in the pure nature, you will no longer run to seek outside, but will return home.

Originally not an illusion, it became an illusion.

Vietnamese translation: The mind is enlightened, all defilements are cleared, the breath turns into a halo that shines throughout the ten directions of the world. I attained Arhatship. The World-Honored One predicted that I would achieve Bodhi.

Lecture: The mind is enlightened, all defilements are gone. When your breath becomes white, your mind suddenly becomes enlightened, clean of all defilements. Every breath in and out turns into a halo that shines throughout the world in all ten directions. I attained Arhatship. At first my breath was like smoke, then it became white like the white point of light on the tip of my nose, and finally it turned into a halo! The light shines throughout the dharma realm in the ten directions. The World-Honored One predicted that I would achieve Bodhi. The Buddha said that in the future, you will definitely become a Buddha.

Phu-long-na Didal-lani Tu

Sutras: 富樓那彌多羅尼子即從座起。頂禮佛足而白佛言。我曠劫來辯才無礙。宣說苦空深達實相。如是乃至恒沙如來。祕密_ _TAG6__法門我於眾中。微妙開示得無所畏。

Transcription: Phu-long-na Didal-lani Tu means following the throne. I pay my respects to the Buddha and recite the Buddha's words. I have no problem with my eloquence. Proclaiming the emptiness of suffering, deeply understanding the true nature. As the secret Dharma of the Tathagata is always known, I believe in the wonderful Dharma Talk and gain no fear.

Vietnamese translation: Phu-long-na Didal-la-ni Zi immediately stood up from his seat, bowed close to the Buddha's feet and told the Buddha, "For many lifetimes up to now, I have been able to speak without hesitation. I have preached the dharmas of suffering and emptiness, deeply attaining the true form. Thus, until the Tathagata's secret dharmas are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, I have used the Dharma Talk method in them. I have achieved the power of fearlessness."

Lecture: Purnamaitreyaniputra is the name of the father's and mother's surnames. Pūrṇa means Man-滿 which is the father's surname. Didalani–Maitreyani means From 慈; Putra means child (子zi). So his name means son of the one with great compassion.

He immediately stood up from his seat, bowed close to the Buddha's feet, and said to the Buddha, "I have been able to preach to you for many lifetimes without hesitation.

There are four types of unhindered eloquence:
1. The Dharma without hindrance 法無礙辯: having the ability to explain all dharmas in a comprehensive and unobstructed way.
2. Meaning without hindrance 義無礙辯: having the ability to explain the meaning of all dharmas without hindrance.
3. Unobstructed words 辭無礙辯: Having the ability to use one sentence, one word, to express countless mysterious meanings in an unobstructed way. It is also capable of condensing countless wonderful meanings into one word, one sentence
4. Unobstructed preaching 樂說無礙辯: Has the ability to adapt to the joy and happiness of all Sentient Beings, skillfully using various means to preach the Dharma to everyone without tiring or boring.

Phu-long-na Didal-ani Tu, unlike Chau-li-Panda, refused to preach the Dharma when he was already a Tripitaka Dharma Master. And as a result, he became stupid. Phu-long-na was not like that, he was very happy in preaching the Dharma.

I preach the dharma of suffering and emptiness, attaining the true nature.

He clearly explained the impermanent, suffering, empty, and non-self nature of all dharmas. To clearly explain the wonderful truth of the true form of all dharmas, the true form is formless, but there is no dharma that does not have a form.

Thus, even though the Tathagata's secret methods are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, I use the Dharma Talk method in them.

Fu-long-na can explain the wonderful secret dharmas of the Tathagata and make them penetrate the profound meaning.

I have gained the power of fearlessness. I have achieved the ability to mock and argue skillfully and fearlessly.

Text: 世尊知我有大辯才。以音聲輪教我發揚。我於佛前助佛轉輪。因師子吼成阿 羅漢。世尊印我說法無上。

Transcription: The World-Honored One knows that the self has great eloquence, uses the wheel of sound, teaches the self to develop. The ego of the Buddha assisted the Buddha in turning the wheel, and the lion's roar became an Arhat. The World-Honored One preaches the supreme Dharma.

Vietnamese translation: The World-Honored One knows that I have a talent for preaching, so I use the sound wheel of Dharma to teach me to promote the Dharma. I followed and helped the Buddha turn the wheel of Dharma. Thanks to the Dharma's sound like a lion's voice, I became an Arhat. The World-Honored One gave me proof that he preaches the Dharma at the highest level.

Lecture: Phu-long-na achieves the path and fruition thanks to tongue-consciousness. He became like that thanks to his diligence in preaching the Dharma. So you see, you can attain enlightenment and attain enlightenment through diligently preaching the Dharma. All you need to do is go deeply into the method you are practicing. Decide decisively on a method and practice diligently. Don't distract your mind when practicing, apply this method today, change to that method tomorrow, then change your mind the next day and choose another method. When you change like that, you just waste time, and you never penetrate any practice at all. You must definitely choose a method and diligently practice it.

The World-Honored One knew that I had a talent for preaching, so he used the sound of the Dharma wheel to teach me to promote the Dharma. There is no one who can argue better than Phu-long-na. When he preached the Dharma, the sound was full and echoed very strongly. With a crowd of about a thousand or ten thousand people, without needing a microphone or loudspeaker, they can still hear very easily. “Buddha taught you to preach the sutras and preach the Dharma.” I followed and helped the Buddha turn the wheel of Dharma. Thanks to the Dharma's sound like a lion's voice, I became an Arhat. I will extol the Buddha's teachings, my teachings will be like the roar of a lion. When the lion roars, other creatures are afraid.

When the demons and pagans heard this roar, they all submitted. The World-Honored One gave me proof that he preaches the Dharma at the highest level.

Text: 佛問圓通我以法音。降伏魔怨銷滅諸漏斯為第一 。
