U-ba-ly

Sutras: 優波離即從座起。頂禮佛足而白佛言。我親隨佛踰城出家。親觀如來六年勤苦。親見如來降伏諸魔制諸外道。解脫世間貪欲諸漏

Transcription: U-ba-ly means following the throne, bowing to Buddha's son and saying Buddha's words. The ego depends on the Buddha to become a monk. Contemplating the Tathagata for six years requires suffering. The view of the Tathagata subdues demons, suppresses heretics, and liberates the world from greed and lust.

Vietnamese translation: Up-ba-ly immediately stood up from his seat, bowed close to the Buddha's feet and told the Buddha, "I have been able to follow the Buddha and become a monk. I have personally seen the Tathagata six years of diligent asceticism, personally seen the Tathagata subdue the demons, tame the pagans, and completely liberate all worldly desires."

Lecture: Upa-li is the best person who maintains the precepts. His name in Sanskrit means superior leader. He never broke even the smallest precepts. His name when he was a Lay Buddhist was Channa (Xan-nac 車匿). He was the one who together with the Crown Prince left the palace and went to the forest to become a monk. He was very familiar with the events in the Buddha's life because he was the person who lived with the Buddha the longest. When the five monks (the five brothers Kieu-tran-na) left the Buddha, Up-ba-ly did not go but remained with him and helped the Crown Prince while he was cultivating. Up-ba-ly immediately stood up from his seat, bowed close to the Buddha's feet and told the Buddha, "I am allowed to follow the Buddha to become a monk. At that time, Up-ba-ly, who was not yet a monk, also known as Xa-nac, first followed the Prince to the city gate towards the East. The Prince was very happy at that time, because staying in the palace for a long time was very boring. He saw a woman giving birth to a baby on the side of the road. She was crying and wailing in pain. The prince asked Xa-nac, “What is it? Why is she crying in such pain?” When Xa-nac finished explaining, the Crown Prince was moved and realized that birth has a lot to do with suffering. After the mother gave birth and the baby was born, the Prince felt no more joy so he told Xa-nac, "Let's go back!" That's enough for today!”

The next day they went together to the south gate. The prince saw an old man. His head shook, his eyes were blurry, his teeth were gone, and he could barely walk. The Crown Prince asked Xa-nac, "What's wrong with that person?"
– That person is too old. Xa-nac replied.
– Oh! –The Crown Prince exclaimed–Is that such an old person! It's so miserable.

This time again, the Crown Prince did not want to go anywhere anymore, so he told Xa-nac to return.

On the third day, when they went to the west gate of the city, they saw a man suffering from a very serious illness. The prince asked Xa-nac, "Why is that person's body so terrible?" Xa-nac replied, “He is sick.” Once again, the Crown Prince felt pity in his heart and did not want to go out anymore.

On the fourth day, they went to the north gate and saw a man who had just died. When the Crown Prince asked about this event, Xa-nac presented the end of human life – death – as such.

The Crown Prince was stunned by the scenes he had just seen, giving birth to old age, illness, and death. At that time, a monk wearing a ka-sa robe passed by. When the Prince saw the monk, he asked who was that Xa-nac? Xa-nac replied:
– Please ask him to hear the explanation.

The Crown Prince, later known as Shakyamuni Buddha, immediately asked the monk:
– Who are you?
– I am a monk.
– What does it mean?
– A person who has given up family life and practiced Buddhism is called a bhikkhu. They became monks hoping to escape the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness and death. Once we have entered the Path, we will see that there is no more birth and no more death – so we are no longer subject to birth or death, we can attain enlightenment.
– Can you tell me how to become a monk? Can you accept me as a disciple?

Bhikkhus are originally gods from the Heaven of Pure Dwelling. The seven causes and conditions were ripe, and he immediately incarnated to meet Shakyamuni Buddha in the middle of the road. When the Prince asked the monk to become his teacher, the monk immediately dropped his stick to the ground and flew back to heaven. The prince had no way to study Buddhism and did not know how to become a monk, so he had no choice but to return to the palace.

At that time, a fortune teller who read the Crown Prince's appearance told the King, "Within the next seven days, if the Crown Prince does not become a monk, he will become a Holy Chakravartin King, and he will rule over all the kingdoms of the world. What Your Majesty needs to do is to keep the Crown Prince in the palace for the next seven days."

From then on, King Tinh Phan kept watch and sent the musketeers to guard around the royal palace, cutting off all means of entering and leaving the palace. A curfew was issued and no one was allowed to enter or leave the palace. Thus, the Crown Prince was kept under house arrest and guarded at all times. In this way, King Tinh Phan hoped that his son, Prince Siddhartha, would attain the position of a Holy Chakravartin King.

The Holy King Chakravarti is the ruler of the four continents of the world: Eastern Thang Than Chau, Western Niu Hoa Chau, Southern Thiem Bo Chau and Bac Cau Lu Chau. A world system includes these four great continents, a sun, a moon and Mount Tu-di. One thousand microcosm worlds are one mesocosm world, one thousand mesocosm worlds are called one macrocosm worlds. This is the meaning of the Three Thousand Great Thousand Worlds. A Holy Chakravartin King rules a small world.

The Prince had great good roots, so even though he was being watched very closely, he was still not confused. King Tinh Phan brought many beautiful women to the Crown Prince's palace. But the prince still looked at them with indifferent eyes, as if he did not see, as if he did not hear. It's true:
The eyes see color but in the mind there is nothing.
The ears hear the sound but the mind doesn't know it.

Or:
There is no body or mind inside,
Outside there is a world.

Then the angel in the Pure Land heaven appeared again and told the Prince, "Prince, have you indulged in the five worldly pleasures and forgotten the vows you made in your previous life? Do you still remember your vows in your previous life?"

Prince Siddhartha replied, "I have not forgotten, but now I do not know how to fulfill that vow."

The angel in the Pure Land Heaven said again, "If you do not forget your vow, and still intend to become a monk, I will help you."
The Crown Prince said, “That's very good!”

The angel told Xa-nac–which means Up-ba-ly that we are now talking about–to prepare the horses, then told the Crown Prince and Xa-nac to go behind the palace garden to hide. At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings appeared, each one holding one horse's leg and then lifting the horse and chariot, the Crown Prince and Up-ba-ly into the air and flying with them. They crossed the clouds and rode the fog for more than 3 yojanas and then stopped in the Snow Mountain.

The prince practiced as soon as he arrived at the mountain. As the angel promised, there was enough rice and sesame there. Every day the Crown Prince uses one sesame seed to live. Then three people from his father's family and two people from his mother's family came to practice with him. There were three people who could not bear the hardships of the monastic life, so they began to doubt, "If we practice suffering like this, when will we become Buddhas? Go home!" These three people left and went to Deer Park to practice. Later, a goddess offered a bowl of milk to the Crown Prince, because she saw that his body was only skin and bones. After drinking milk, he found his body became normal. But the two people who remained to practice with him saw this and thought, "Before, the Crown Prince could endure asceticism, but now he can no longer endure it.

If the prince drinks milk, he will not achieve anything. The Crown Prince should not have used that thing. Let's go!” So those close to him from his father's family and mother's family left him, leaving only Up-ba-ly. So Upa-ly said, "It was I who crossed the city with the Buddha to become a monk. I was with him in the royal garden when he got on his horse to leave the city. I personally saw the Tathagata six years of diligent asceticism, for six years he endured asceticism, endured difficult things. I personally saw the Tathagata subdue the demons, subdue the heretics and completely liberate all worldly desires. The Crown Prince should have become a Buddha right while he was still in the Snow Mountain, but he was still afraid that Sentient Beings of future generations will misunderstand that, to become Buddhas, they must practice extreme asceticism. Therefore, he no longer meditated in the deserted mountain but went to the Bodhi tree, he sat under this tree and vowed that he would not leave the tree until he became a Buddha.

After the Buddha sat meditating under the Bodhi tree for 49 days, the demon king in the Six Desire Heavens was warned in a dream. He dreamed that there were 32 incarnations. When he woke up, he meditated to find out the cause of the dream. He discovered that there was a Bodhisattva meditating under the Bodhi tree and was about to become a Buddha. He thought, "This cannot happen. I must find a way to destroy this person's concentration." He immediately sent four witches, they were all very beautiful. Demons are monsters, but they also don't like ugliness. They were sent to disturb Buddha Shakyamuni's concentration by displaying 32 very attractive transformations.

They tried to seduce Shakyamuni Buddha. They wanted the Buddha to also have ordinary thoughts of desire and abandon concentration. They wanted to stimulate the Buddha's desire. But Buddha neither liked them nor hated them. Even though he is not straw or wood or stone, as the folk saying goes, "He is not wood or stone, how can he be heartless?" But the Buddha overcame these experiences and was never swayed by them. He was not swayed by the magical power of this demon girl. He remained in a state of immobility. His mind was not moved at all, he never had thoughts of desire.

Encountering these scenes, he did not have thoughts. At this time, the Buddha contemplated impurity, similar to the nine topics mentioned above (Nine Contemplations). He thought, “Oh! You come to test me. Even though you are very beautiful now, you will become dry bones. The nine acupuncture points on your body constantly secrete impure things. The eyes secrete gunk, the ears secrete wax, the nose secretes mucus, the mouth secretes phlegm, all dirty things. In addition, your body also secretes feces and urine, making you even dirtier. In addition, there are many germs in every pore of your body.

That whole body is a foul substance.” His contemplation turned to seeing four beautiful girls become four old witches. They looked at each other and saw that each person's skin was as wrinkled as a chicken's leg and their hair was as white as a crane's feathers. Their noses were runny and their mouths were full of drool. Their bodies were extremely emaciated. They looked at each other and started to feel disgusted. Realizing that they had become old and could no longer deceive the Buddha, they left. When the demon king saw that the four female ghosts had returned defeated, he personally commanded his children and grandchildren to come and kill the Buddha. But Buddha remained motionless. He is not afraid. He entered the Samadhi of Non-avoidance. If your mind wavers, demons will harm you. If your mind is motionless, it cannot do anything to you.

There was another pagan named Shen Mu 申目 (Shen Jih) who mixed poison in food and then offered it to Buddha. When the Buddha saw the food, he thought, “I pray that, just as there is nothing poisonous in my mind, then when I eat this food, it will not harm me.” Then eat that Chapter.

Other pagans were jealous of the Buddha. Before the Buddha reached this realm, the Brahmin priests were considered supreme. Everyone turns to them. But after the Buddha practiced asceticism for six years and attained enlightenment, the disciples of non-Buddhists all turned to the Buddha. Like Kasyapa, Maudgalyayana, and Sariputta were all once disciples of heretical sects. That's why the leaders of the pagan groups were very jealous. They fed the crazy elephants–five such crazy elephants–and released them to harm the Buddha. Who would have thought that when the 5 fierce elephants approached the Buddha, he opened his hand and 5 lions appeared from his 5 fingers, the 5 crazy elephants trembled in fear to the point of death. The Buddha's ability to subdue demons and pagans is truly great.

He also conquered desire. Love is the hardest thing to conquer. It makes people live like drunkards and die in dreams. If you cannot eliminate craving, then you cannot eliminate defilements. You still have defilements because you still have craving. Sentient Beings are all immersed in lust.

Heavy love karma is Sentient Beings.
The karma of ending love is not Buddhas.

The Buddhas became Buddhas because they had put an end to all desires. Sentient Beings will forever be Sentient Beings because their craving karma is so deep that they cannot escape the bondage of samsara, causing them to drift in the three worlds.
If there is no longer any defilement, then:
The vast sea of suffering,
Turn around and see the shore.
It is a complete escape from worldly desires.

Text: 承佛教戒,如是乃至三千威儀八萬微細。性業遮業悉皆清淨。身心寂滅成阿羅漢。

Transcription: Inheriting the Buddhist precepts, like the three thousand majestic majesty of the world, eight thousand subtleties, the nature of karma is completely pure. Body and mind pass away and become Arhat.

Vietnamese translation: I rely on the precepts taught by the Buddha, so my three thousand majestic postures, eighty thousand virtuous actions, down to the nature of karma, the price of karma are all pure. My body and mind will be quiet and I will become an Arhat.

Lecture: I rely on the precepts taught by the Buddha. Up-ba-ly personally followed the Buddha since he became a monk. Up-ba-ly himself saw the Buddha practicing asceticism for six years in the Snow Mountain; It was Upali who saw the Buddha sitting under the Bodhi tree, and attained enlightenment when he saw the morning star rising; It was Up-ba-ly who saw the Buddha subdue the demons of pagans, until he achieved Buddhahood. Upa-li all witnessed those events. After Shakyamuni Buddha attained enlightenment, he began to teach the dharma that he had realized. He saw that Upa-li was the most skillful in keeping the precepts in the great assembly from countless Buddhas of the past. When Shakyamuni Buddha appeared in the Saha world and practiced and accomplished his karma, Upabali also immediately appeared in this world. Therefore, the Buddha taught Upa-ly to focus on practicing the precepts in the Buddha Dharma.

Now I will explain the precepts, and you are all Buddhists who are studying Buddhism so you must listen carefully.

First are the five precepts:
1. Do not kill.
2. Do not steal.
3. Do not commit adultery.
4. Don't lie.
5. Don't drink alcohol.

Next are the 8 precepts, including the 5 precepts mentioned before, along with the 3 precepts,
6. Do not decorate your body with perfume or perfume.
7. Do not sit on a high or wide bed; and do not watch or listen to music. By not lying or sitting on a high or wide bed, you will eliminate your pride and arrogance.
8. Do not eat at improper times.

Not eating at the wrong time means not eating after noon. Not eating after noon helps you control your greed, because if you want to eat whenever you like, you will like to eat all the time. Lay Buddhists should keep this precept.

Novices have 10 precepts that are different from the precepts of lay Buddhists. It is not true that after receiving the 5 precepts, you are considered a member of the Sangha. Keeping the 8 precepts is not considered a member of the Sangha. People who receive the 10 major precepts and 48 minor precepts of the Bodhisattva precepts are not considered members of the sangha. To be a member of the Sangha, you must first take 10 novice precepts, then 250 bhikkhu precepts, or 348 bhikshuni precepts, and an additional 10 major and 48 minor precepts of the Bodhisattva precepts. It's not like you're in America today and want to establish a different way.

You cannot create another system of precepts and say, “Everyone is a member of the Sangha.” I have heard that even the tables and chairs are members of the sangha! Cups, cups, chopsticks, and chopsticks are also members of the Sangha–everything is the Sangha! This is truly strange–unspeakably strange. In this case, there is nothing in the entire world that is not a Sangha. If the entire universe and all things are Sangha, then why does the Sangha have to harmonize with each other to form? I found this to be something I had never heard of before–it was truly unprecedented.

The word ‘precepts’ comes from the Sanskrit word prātimokṣa. Also called śīla. The meaning in Chinese is to prevent evil.

Evil people act
They serve well

One day, an elderly Upasaka asked an elder Bodhisattva who had been a monk for many years how to practice the Way. The elder replied, "Do not do evil. Be diligent in doing good."

The elderly Upasaka said. "I don't need you to explain that. Even a three-year-old child knows that."

The elder explained, “A three-year-old child can know that, but an eighty-year-old man will not do this.”

In this day and age, some people form groups and call themselves 'Sangha'. Let's see how many precepts they keep? If you do not keep the precepts completely, you cannot be called a Sangha. If they object and say that they are different and newly reformed, then they should not call themselves Buddhist. If they still do not respect and cling to the age-old precepts of Buddhism, then what is the Buddhism they are following? They will answer, “New-Buddhists.” Then ask them what's new in it? The Buddha himself has the ability to teach the Dharma in heaven and hell, he has the ability to teach in the human world and even go to the dragon palace to preach the Dharma. So where do these people of New Buddhism preach the Dharma? Ask them that.

They would answer, "It's a myth. Of course we can't go there. You can create your own myth. You just live with the myth."

If someone has the same ability as any of my disciples (who have opened the five eyes) in this assembly, they still do not have the right to change the foundation of Buddhist teachings, and they still cannot show that they are too intelligent and flexible. What right do they have to change Buddhism? When you do business, you must have capital. If you want to be a high official in the government, you must study and get a degree. If these people want to establish New Buddhism, what is their foundation?

Their response would be, "We teach the teachings of the Four Noble Truths of the Buddha, teach the Six Noble Truths, teach the twelve causes and conditions, and recite the Buddha's mantras. We recite the Buddha's sutras."

Ask them again, “If you read Buddhist scriptures and recite Buddha's mantras, what is new?” That is truly a paradox.

I hope that Buddhists in America will make an effort to respond to these mistakes. Otherwise, the decline of the Dharma will certainly occur. Buddha Shakyamuni predicted that in the Dharma Ending Age, demon children and grandchildren will come to this world with great power. When Shakyamuni Buddha subdued the demon king and accepted the pagan, the demon Batam, he knew about this. It says, “I know I can't do anything to you now, but in the future I will destroy your teachings.”

Buddha asked again, “How did you do that?”

"I will let my descendants sneak into your Sangha. Eat and drink like you, wear robes like you, and urinate and urinate into your bowls. My descendants will destroy the Dharma from within your Sangha."

Buddha Shakyamuni long ago saw what is happening today.

They wear Tathagata's robes.
They use Tathagata's Chapter.
But in Buddhism, they do not do exactly what Buddha did.

Upa-li was the foremost keeper of precepts among the Buddha's disciples. In Buddhism, there are Lawyers who specialize in strictly maintaining the precepts, and there are Dharma Masters who specialize in preaching sutras and teachings. Shamans have two meanings: one is those who specialize in teaching the Dharma to others, and the other is someone who accepts the Dharma as their teacher, they study the sutras to practice. There are also Zen masters, they specialize in meditation and meditation.

When Shakyamuni Buddha was still alive, all Sentient Beings relied on the Buddha as their guiding teacher. When the Buddha passed away, he advised monks and nuns to accept the precepts as teachers. Therefore, the most important thing for monks and nuns is to strictly maintain the precepts. Lawyers like Mr. Up-ba-ly are especially strict with the precepts. He said, I rely on the precepts taught by the Buddha, so I have three thousand majesty,

The number three thousand postures comes from the 250 precepts of a monk multiplied by the four postures – walking, standing, lying, sitting, to 1000; Multiply by 3 karma, body, speech, and mind, to get 3000.

Each posture of walking, standing, lying, and sitting has its own special characteristics.

1. Go like the wind. This wind is not a hurricane, but like a light breath, like the autumn wind. You should walk slowly with a steady style, not in a hurry like running forward.
2. Stand like a pine tree: Stand straight like a pine tree, without leaning or leaning from one side to the other.
3. Sit like a bell: Sit like a big, heavy bell that hangs firmly and does not move.
4. Lie like a bow: You should lie in an auspicious position, lying on your right side, right hand placed on the right cheek and left hand placed along the left leg.

Eighty thousand virtues, Eighty thousand is a round number. Only give eighty-four thousand acts of kindness. This number is due to the 3000 postures of body, speech and mind multiplied by 7 (seven senses; body 3, speech 4) to become 21,000, multiplied by 4 (four equal parts: greed, anger, ignorance, equal parts) which is 84,000.

Upa-li continues to present the nature of karma and the price of karma are all pure. Direct karma refers to the four basic silent precepts: killing, lust, and false speech. Any action belonging to these 4 things is a violation and an immediate violation of the precepts. If anyone violates one of these four precepts, they will no longer have the opportunity to repent.
